review: 701.54c-3, 701.54c-4: with three or four temptations the Ring's loot trigger also fires when Grizzly Bears attacks, but A's library was empty, so A would draw from an empty library and lose; gave A a library with Island on top and added the loot to decisions and every expected outcome.

701.54d-1: the b_tempted variant changed both the active player and the caster and tested only Ringwraiths' 'you' condition, not 701.54d; replaced it with has_creature (the same temptation with a creature to choose), dropped B's now-unused cards, and noted that 701.54d has no does_not_fire branch.
701.54b-1: 701.54b (Ring-bearer is not copiable) has an observable outcome through copy effects but was triaged definitional; reclassified as mechanical/continuous and added a Clone scenario.

scenarios.title: Each time the Ring tempts a player a creature becomes Ring-bearer until another one does

setup.notes: The Ring has tempted A once and Grizzly Bears is A's Ring-bearer. Library lists are top first; cards below the listed ones are irrelevant Forests. The Ring emblem and the Ring-bearer designation are not zones or fields the scenario format lists, so they are described here.

decisions: A casts Birthday Escape, tapping the Island.
Both players pass; Birthday Escape resolves: A draws a card, then the Ring tempts A.
A chooses Runeclaw Bear as the new Ring-bearer.

variants.label: new_bearer
variants.expected: The Ring has tempted A twice. Runeclaw Bear is A's Ring-bearer (and legendary) and Grizzly Bears is no longer a Ring-bearer. A drew Forest.

variants.label: same_bearer
variants.expected: The Ring has tempted A twice. Grizzly Bears is still A's Ring-bearer and Runeclaw Bear is not. A drew Forest.

scenarios.title: The Ring makes the Ring-bearer legendary and unblockable by creatures with greater power

setup.notes: The Ring has tempted A once and Grizzly Bears (2/2) is A's Ring-bearer. Hill Giant is 3/3. The Ring emblem and the Ring-bearer designation are not zones or fields the scenario format lists, so they are described here.

decisions: A attacks B with Grizzly Bears.
B's blocks are declared: Hill Giant is considered as a blocker.

variants.label: greater_power
variants.expected: Grizzly Bears is legendary. Hill Giant (power 3) cannot block Grizzly Bears (power 2): the block is illegal.

variants.label: equal_power
variants.delta: B's creature is Runeclaw Bear (2/2) instead of Hill Giant.
variants.expected: Runeclaw Bear (power 2, not greater than 2) can legally block Grizzly Bears.

variants.label: not_bearer
variants.delta: A attacks with Runeclaw Bear, which is not the Ring-bearer, and B's creature is Hill Giant.
variants.expected: Runeclaw Bear has no Ring evasion: Hill Giant can legally block it.

scenarios.title: After two temptations the Ring-bearer attacking makes its controller loot

setup.notes: The Ring has tempted A twice and Grizzly Bears is A's Ring-bearer. Library lists are top first; cards below the listed ones are irrelevant Forests. The Ring emblem and the Ring-bearer designation are not zones or fields the scenario format lists, so they are described here.

decisions: A attacks B with Grizzly Bears.
The Ring's attack trigger resolves: A draws a card, then discards Forest.

variants.label: two_temptations
variants.expected: The trigger fires: A draws Island and discards Forest. A's hand is [Island] and Forest is in A's graveyard.

variants.label: one_temptation
variants.delta: The Ring has tempted A only once.
variants.expected: No trigger fires. A's hand stays [Forest] and Island stays on top of the library.

variants.label: not_bearer
variants.delta: A attacks with Runeclaw Bear, which is not the Ring-bearer.
variants.expected: No trigger fires. A's hand stays [Forest] and Island stays on top of the library.

scenarios.title: After three temptations a creature blocking the Ring-bearer is sacrificed at end of combat

setup.notes: The Ring has tempted A three times and Grizzly Bears (2/2) is A's Ring-bearer. Wall of Wood is 0/3 with defender. The Ring emblem and the Ring-bearer designation are not zones or fields the scenario format lists, so they are described here. Library lists are top first; cards below the listed ones are irrelevant Forests.

decisions: A attacks B with Grizzly Bears.
The Ring's attack trigger (A has been tempted two or more times) resolves: A draws Island and discards it.
B blocks Grizzly Bears with Wall of Wood; combat damage is dealt, and the end of combat step is reached.

variants.label: three_temptations
variants.expected: Grizzly Bears' attack makes A draw Island and discard it. Wall of Wood takes 2 damage and survives combat damage. At end of combat B sacrifices Wall of Wood: it moves to B's graveyard.

variants.label: two_temptations
variants.delta: The Ring has tempted A only twice.
variants.expected: Grizzly Bears' attack makes A draw Island and discard it. Wall of Wood takes 2 damage and survives combat. Nothing is sacrificed: it stays on the battlefield with 2 damage marked until the cleanup step.

scenarios.title: After four temptations the Ring-bearer's combat damage to a player makes each opponent lose 3 life

setup.notes: The Ring has tempted A four times and Grizzly Bears is A's Ring-bearer. The Ring emblem and the Ring-bearer designation are not zones or fields the scenario format lists, so they are described here. Library lists are top first; cards below the listed ones are irrelevant Forests.

decisions: A attacks B with Grizzly Bears. B has no blockers.
The Ring's attack trigger (A has been tempted two or more times) resolves: A draws Island and discards it.
Combat damage is dealt and the Ring's trigger resolves.

variants.label: four_temptations
variants.expected: Grizzly Bears' attack makes A draw Island and discard it. Grizzly Bears deals 2 combat damage to B and the Ring's trigger makes B lose 3 life: B's life is 15.

variants.label: three_temptations
variants.delta: The Ring has tempted A only three times.
variants.expected: Grizzly Bears' attack makes A draw Island and discard it. Grizzly Bears deals 2 combat damage to B and no trigger fires: B's life is 18.

scenarios.title: The Ring tempts a player, firing temptation triggers, even if there is no creature to choose

setup.notes: A controls no creature. Ringwraiths in A's graveyard: when the Ring tempts you, return it from your graveyard to your hand. Library lists are top first; cards below the listed ones are irrelevant Forests. The Ring emblem and the Ring-bearer designation are not zones or fields the scenario format lists, so they are described here.

decisions: A casts Birthday Escape, tapping the Island.
Both players pass; Birthday Escape resolves: A draws a card, then the Ring tempts A. A has no creature to choose as Ring-bearer.
Ringwraiths' trigger resolves if it fired.

variants.label: no_creature
variants.expected: A gets the Ring emblem and has no Ring-bearer, but the Ring still tempted A: Ringwraiths' trigger fires and Ringwraiths returns from A's graveyard to A's hand. A drew Forest.

variants.label: has_creature
variants.delta: A controls Grizzly Bears, which A chooses as Ring-bearer.
variants.expected: A gets the Ring emblem and Grizzly Bears becomes A's Ring-bearer (legendary). Ringwraiths' trigger fires and Ringwraiths returns to A's hand. A drew Forest.

scenarios.forge_notes: 701.54d has no does_not_fire branch: completing the actions of 701.54a always counts as the Ring tempting the player.

scenarios.title: A creature is your Ring-bearer only while it is on the battlefield under your control

setup.notes: The Ring has tempted A once and Grizzly Bears is A's Ring-bearer (legendary). Active player is B. The Ring emblem and the Ring-bearer designation are not zones or fields the scenario format lists, so they are described here.

decisions: B casts Act of Treason targeting Grizzly Bears, tapping three Mountains.
Both players pass; Act of Treason resolves: B gains control of Grizzly Bears until end of turn, untaps it and it gains haste.
The turn ends and control of Grizzly Bears returns to A.

variants.label: bearer_stolen
variants.expected: While B controls Grizzly Bears it is not A's Ring-bearer, so it is no longer legendary. After control returns to A it is still not a Ring-bearer: A has no Ring-bearer.

variants.label: other_creature_stolen
variants.delta: B targets Runeclaw Bear with Act of Treason.
variants.expected: Grizzly Bears stays A's Ring-bearer and legendary. Runeclaw Bear is controlled by B until end of turn and is not a Ring-bearer.

scenarios.title: A copy of the Ring-bearer is not a Ring-bearer

setup.notes: The Ring has tempted A once and Grizzly Bears is A's Ring-bearer, so it is legendary through the Ring emblem. The Ring emblem and the Ring-bearer designation are not zones or fields the scenario format lists, so they are described here.

decisions: A casts Clone, tapping four Islands.
Both players pass; Clone resolves and A has it enter as a copy of A's Ring-bearer.
If the legend rule applies, A keeps the original creature.

variants.label: copy_of_bearer
variants.expected: Clone enters as Grizzly Bears, a 2/2 that is neither legendary nor a Ring-bearer. Both creatures stay on the battlefield and the original Grizzly Bears is still A's Ring-bearer.

variants.label: printed_legendary
variants.delta: A's Ring-bearer is Isamaru, Hound of Konda (a printed legendary 2/2) instead of Grizzly Bears.
variants.expected: Clone enters as Isamaru, Hound of Konda, legendary because that supertype is copiable, but not a Ring-bearer. The legend rule puts the Clone into A's graveyard; the original Isamaru stays A's Ring-bearer.

scenarios.forge_notes: 701.54b has no does_not_fire branch: the designation is never copied. The printed_legendary variant contrasts it with a copiable supertype.
